# 續佛祖統紀

**ID:** X1515
**Volume:** X75
**Category:** 史傳部類
**Original Category:** 史傳部／編年通史
**Juans:** 2
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/X1515

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A short two-juan continuation of [志磐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BF%97%E7%A3%90)'s monumental *Fózǔ tǒngjì* ([KR6r0012](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0012)), preserved anonymously in the *Manji Xuzangjing* (X75 no. 1515). The compiler is unnamed in the surviving text. The work continues the Tiāntái universal-history project from the point at which [志磐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BF%97%E7%A3%90) broke off (1236) into the Yuán dynasty, and is composed from a Tiāntái sectarian standpoint.

**Abstract**

The work consists of two juan: a biographical/annalistic supplement covering Buddhist events of the late Sòng and early to mid Yuán, and a series of biographical entries on Tiāntái masters of the period 1240–1340 or thereabouts. Without internal evidence the dating cannot be tightened beyond the bracket 1270 (post-Zhìpán) to 1340 (latest events apparently recorded). The compiler was clearly a Tiāntái monk in the Sìmíng 四明 lineage; some scholars have tentatively associated the work with the circle around the early-Yuán Tiāntái historian Méng Rùn 蒙潤 (1275–1342).

The text is short, uneven in quality, and was little circulated. Its principal value is as a Tiāntái-aligned record of Buddhist events for the Yuán transition, supplementing the more universalising accounts of [念常](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%BF%B5%E5%B8%B8) in [KR6r0013](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0013) and the chronicle in [覺岸](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%A6%BA%E5%B2%B8)'s [KR6r0014](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6r/KR6r0014).
